title: Mastering Retinitis Pigmentosa (RP): A Comprehensive Clinical Atlas
summary: Retinitis Pigmentosa (RP) represents a genetically heterogeneous group of inherited retinal dystrophies characterized by progressive degeneration of photoreceptors, beginning with rod-cone dystrophy. This guide covers the pathophysiological, diagnostic, and clinical landscape for the modern ophthalmologist.

sections.title: Definition & Pathophysiology
sections.content: RP is a primary dystrophy of the retinal photoreceptors (rods > cones) and retinal pigment epithelium (RPE). Pathophysiology typically involves mutations in genes responsible for the phototransduction cascade, structural integrity (e.g., Rhodopsin, peripherin-2), or RPE metabolism. Common outcomes include apoptosis of rods followed by secondary cone death due to oxidative stress, nutrient deprivation, and toxic byproduct accumulation.

sections.title: Classic Clinical Triad
content: 1. Bone-spicule intraretinal pigmentary changes
2. Attenuation of retinal arterioles
3. Waxy pallor of the optic disc

sections.title: Diagnostic Workup Protocol
content: Step 1: Full clinical history (including systemic syndromes like Usher or Bassen-Kornzweig).
Step 2: Goldmann Visual Fields (typically show mid-peripheral scotomas progressing to ring scotomas).
Step 3: Full-field ERG (scotopic b-wave reduction is the hallmark, often preceding visible fundus changes).
Step 4: SD-OCT (measures ellipsoid zone loss and central retinal thickness).
Step 5: Fundus Autofluorescence (FAF) to assess RPE integrity/hyperautofluorescent rings.
Step 6: Genetic Testing (Next-Generation Sequencing/Panel testing).

rows: Rapid onset, associated with systemic malignancy

sections.title: Red Flags: When to refer urgently
content: Sudden, unilateral vision loss (consider macular edema or rhegmatogenous RD).
Cystoid Macular Edema (CME) not responsive to topical dorzolamide.
Signs of associated systemic vasculitis or malignancy.
New-onset nyctalopia that progresses rapidly in childhood (consider syndromic association).

content.explanation: Bone-spicules (pigmentation), Arteriolar attenuation, Waxy optic disc.

sections.title: Management Framework
content: Vitamin A Palmitate (15,000 IU/day) - Controversial, monitor liver function.
DHA/Omega-3 supplements (modest benefits in some cohorts).
Topical CAIs (Dorzolamide 2%) for CME treatment.
Low vision aids and vocational rehabilitation.
Voretigene neparvovec (Luxturna) for RPE65 mutation-associated disease.
Retinal prostheses (Argus II) for late-stage patients.

sections.title: Key Clinical Pearls
content: The 'Ring Scotoma' on visual field testing is the classic deficit pattern.
ERG testing remains the gold standard for early diagnosis before symptomatic onset.
Always inquire about hearing loss; Usher syndrome is the most common syndromic cause (RP + sensorineural hearing loss).
Ellipsoid zone (EZ) integrity on OCT is the strongest predictor of visual potential.
The disease is 'progressive'; counseling patients regarding driving status and legal blindness is essential early on.
